questions.q: In the spreadsheet analogy for Salesforce's data model, what does a 'record' correspond to?
options: One row of the spreadsheet — a specific instance like 'Acme Corp'
The entire spreadsheet itself
One column of the spreadsheet
The name of the spreadsheet file
questions.explain: A record is one specific instance of an object — like one row in a spreadsheet, such as the Account record 'Acme Corp.'

options: A type of object, like Account or Contact
One piece of information captured on a record, like Phone or Industry
A specific record's unique ID number only
A tab in the Salesforce navigation bar
questions.explain: A field is one piece of information on a record — like a spreadsheet column, such as Industry or Phone — and it's part of the object's metadata definition.

questions.q: Which of these is a standard object that Salesforce ships with, ready to use?
options: A custom 'Property' object built by a property management company
A custom 'Course' object built by a university
Whatever object name an admin happens to pick
Account
questions.explain: Account is one of Salesforce's built-in standard objects, along with Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and others — no setup required. Custom objects like 'Property' or 'Course' are created by admins for needs standard objects don't cover.

questions.q: Why would a business create a custom object instead of using a standard one?
options: Because custom objects are required before any standard object can be used
Because their data doesn't fit any of the pre-built standard objects, like a university needing to track Courses
Because custom objects are faster to query than standard objects
Because standard objects can only hold ten records at a time
questions.explain: Custom objects exist for business data that doesn't map to any standard object — once created, they behave exactly like standard objects, complete with their own fields, records, and tab.

questions.q: In the Salesforce interface, how do users typically reach a specific object's list of records?
options: By exporting all data to a spreadsheet first
There is no way to browse an object's records directly
Only an admin can view any records, ever
By clicking that object's corresponding tab, such as Accounts or Opportunities
questions.explain: Each object a user has access to typically has a corresponding tab in the interface — clicking it opens a list of that object's records.
